page.layout: One printed page, one text column with no margin notes. Running head at top, page number at top right. Below the last line, the catchword "in" at the right.

main_text.p: opportunè satis poteram, Parlamentum tran-stulissem, gratum scilicet futurum in quocunque loco, nullibi verò, tot diversis & pravis Humoribus obnoxium. Sed hæc omnia Deo relinquenda sunt, qui Sapientiæ suæ Gloriam, miserias & stultitias nostras detegendo illustrat.

p.i: Tu autem Domine refugium mihi & suscep-tor meus ad te confugiam, & in tuto fuero, tu com-pescis strepitum marium, & fremitum populo-rum.
Flumina Domine intraverunt, torrentes pene absorbuissent animam meam.

Intucor[?] peccata mea, & peccata populi mei, (tumultus animarum nostrarum contra Te Domine (ut justam Popularis hujus Diluvii causam, quod ita omnes fidei, modestiae, Legum, Justitiae, Religionis ripas superare & transilire permisisti

Tu vero qui congregas aquas in locum unum, ut arida appareant, & reverti coegisti aquas quae terram obruebant verbo potentiae tuae. Compesce hanc vulgi Belluam & Eripe me à ferocia, & contradictionibus populi.

Reddemobis[?] precamur libertatem consiliorum, & Parlamentorum fac ut nullo affectu occaecati lucem Rationis, & Religionis intucamur, eamque ordine illo & gravitate sequamur quae homines decet & Christianos, sic nomen tuum laudabimus qui es Deus ordinis & consilii.
Quod aut nolit homo, aut nequit reprimere omnipotens tua Justitia & potestas, & velit.
Des Domine his qui adhuc in vivis sunt, aquas[?]

page.notes: Long s rendered as plain s throughout. Several words are unclear: "Intucor" (possibly "Intueor"), "Reddemobis", and the final word "aquas" at the page foot, which looks like "iquas" on the scan, are marked [?]. The opening parenthesis in the paragraph beginning "Intucor" is not closed on the page. Small dots and marks in the lower margin and right edge are stains or show-through and were left out. The catchword "in" is taken from the lower right corner.
